text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian military and Interior Ministry sources said Italy has decided to turn away boats bringing a flood of Albanians to its ports from across the Adriatic. Italy has already sent in some eight tonnes of emergency medical aid requested by Albanian prime minister Bashkim Fino (all).

* A meeting between majority parties is expected to take place today or tomorrow to try and find an agreement over the measures needed for the 15-16 trillion lire mini-budget. Prime minister Romano Prodi is also expected to meet today trade unions and employers' association Confindustria (all).
* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini in an interview says a delay of one year in the start of Emu would be "useful for everybody" (Sole 24 Ore).

* The Italian Treasury said that shareholders in Stet will be able to take a maximum three percent stake in the Italian telecoms group following its privatisation. The Treasury will hold a so-called "golden share" which will give it special voting rights after it loses majority control for up to three years after the sell-off (all).

* A meeting of bankers and the central bank showed that interest margins are expected to fall in 1997 and it will hardly be possible to compensate them with profits from securities operations. Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio reaffirmed it is necessary to contain costs and deal with redundancies which are extimated around 30,000 (all).
* The International Monetary Found reportedly estimates Italy's 1997 deficit/GDP ratio at 4 percent unless a minibudget of 20 trillion lire is launched (Sole 24 Ore).

* The European Commission will postpone its verdict over the 3 trillion lire plan to recapitalise Italy's flag carrier Alitalia. A negative evaluation of the plan has reportedly been formulated by the Commission's advisor Ernst & Young (Sole 24 Ore).

* Italian telecoms systems maker Italtel said it posted a 1996 consolidated net profit of 5 trillion lire against a 1995 loss of 74 billion lire. The group's turnover rose 20 percent to 3.90 trillion lire (all).

* Shares in Parmalat Finanziaria, Italy's largest quoted food group, rose 6.78 percent to 2,315 lire on the Milan stock market after Friday's announcement it was buying a majority stake in Canada's Beatrice Foods.
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
